harvest_notes: Plants must be at least 5 years old with 3 compound leaves. Count stem scars on the root neck to confirm: a 5-year-old plant carries 4 scars. Keep the neck ATTACHED to the root - it is how age is verified, and a root without one cannot be certified for export. WEST VIRGINIA: dig only plants with three or more prongs and no fewer than 15 leaflets, and only when THE BERRIES ARE RED - ripeness is a condition of legal harvest here, not just good practice. Plant the seeds at the root spot. Digging on state forests, state parks and other state land is prohibited; private land needs prior written consent. Possession is prohibited 1 April to 31 August without a Division of Forestry weight receipt, and roots must be sold or weight-receipted by 31 March. Monongahela National Forest permits are available for a fee. Source: WV Division of Forestry Ginseng Program. On federal land: harvest is prohibited in all National Park Service units and national wildlife refuges, and in most national forests.
